blockMcqs.question: What is the primary job of the physical layer?
options: Transmit raw bits as signals on a medium
blockMcqs.explanation: The physical layer moves bits as electrical, optical, or radio signals. It does not interpret or address them.

blockMcqs.question: Which medium is immune to electromagnetic interference?
blockMcqs.explanation: Fiber optic uses light pulses through glass, which are unaffected by electromagnetic interference.

blockMcqs.question: The data link layer provides delivery between which two points?
options: Source host and destination host globally
blockMcqs.explanation: The data link layer is node-to-node (one hop). End-to-end delivery across the internet is handled by the network layer (IP).

blockMcqs.question: How many bits is a MAC address?
blockMcqs.explanation: MAC addresses are 48 bits, written as six hex pairs (e.g. AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF).

blockMcqs.question: What key difference separates a MAC address from an IP address?
options: MAC is 128 bits; IP is 32 bits
MAC is global; IP is local
MAC is link-local; IP is end-to-end global
MAC changes per hop; IP stays constant
blockMcqs.explanation: MAC addresses are used only within a local segment (layer 2). IP addresses route packets end-to-end across networks (layer 3).

blockMcqs.question: What type of message does an ARP request use?
options: Broadcast to all devices on the segment
Multicast to a group of routers
blockMcqs.explanation: ARP sends a broadcast so every device on the local segment receives it. Only the device with the matching IP replies.

blockMcqs.question: Which device breaks a broadcast domain?
blockMcqs.explanation: Routers do not forward broadcast frames, so they separate broadcast domains. Switches and hubs pass broadcasts to all ports.

blockMcqs.question: Why is CSMA/CD largely unused in modern Ethernet?
options: Full-duplex switches give each device a dedicated link
IP handles collision detection at layer 3
blockMcqs.explanation: Full-duplex switched Ethernet gives each port a private link with no shared medium, so simultaneous transmissions cannot collide.
